chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā and Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Indeed, the blood of istiḥāḍah and menstruation do not emerge from one place. Indeed, the blood of istiḥāḍah is cold, and indeed the blood of menstruation is hot.”

key_terms.الْحَيْضِ: menstruation, the legally recognized menstrual bleeding
key_terms.بَارِدٌ: cold, a described quality of istiḥāḍah blood in this report
key_terms.حَارٌّ: hot, a described quality of menstrual blood in this report
key_terms.دَمَ الِاسْتِحَاضَةِ: the blood of istiḥāḍah, irregular non-menstrual bleeding
key_terms.مَكَانٍ وَاحِدٍ: one place, indicating a distinction in origin

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام distinguish between menstrual blood and istiḥāḍah blood?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between the blood of istiḥāḍah and the blood of menstruation by describing a difference in their source and physical quality. It serves as a jurisprudential indicator for differentiating the two conditions in rulings of ritual purity and worship.
